{
  "project_id": "P-GTM-SmartPublicFinances",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Cyberattacks could compromise PFM information systems, causing data loss, service disruption and loss of public trust.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Implement ISO‑27000 ISMS, establish a CSIRT and SOC, conduct regular penetration testing and staff cyber‑security training.",
      "evidence": "Section 10‑11: multiple cyber‑attacks on tax authority (2021), Foreign Ministry (2022), Guatecompras (2023)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Delay in establishing the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) may postpone disbursements and stall reform activities.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Set a firm deadline, monitor PIU staffing weekly, and include PIU establishment as a withdrawal condition with Bank oversight.",
      "evidence": "Condition: No withdrawal until PIU is established (Section ‘Conditions’, withdrawal condition)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Fragmented and non‑interoperable legacy IFMIS and peripheral systems could hinder data integration and efficiency gains.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Adopt a phased integration roadmap, use open standards, and conduct interoperability testing before full rollout.",
      "evidence": "Section 9‑10: fragmentation, manual processes, lack of transactional integration between SICOIN and Guatecompras."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Insufficient data governance and analytics capacity may limit the use of data‑driven decision‑making.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Create a data governance model, establish a dedicated analytics unit, and deliver structured training for data analysts.",
      "evidence": "Section 9‑10: weak data governance, limited analytical capacity, lack of structured career paths."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "High staff turnover and weak institutional stability could erode reform ownership and continuity.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Secure senior‑level commitment, institutionalize reform champions, and implement incentive mechanisms for key staff.",
      "evidence": "Lesson learned (Section 32): lack of preparation and institutional stability caused past reform failures."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Political commitment may wane, leading to reduced support for PFM reforms and possible policy reversals.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Engage high‑level officials through regular briefings, embed reforms in legal frameworks, and build a coalition of ministries.",
      "evidence": "Section 32: importance of sustained senior government leadership for reform success."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Extreme weather events could damage ICT infrastructure, interrupt system operations and delay implementation.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Design infrastructure to be climate‑resilient, locate critical servers in safe zones, and develop a robust business continuity plan.",
      "evidence": "Section 44‑46: climate risks identified; need for business continuity and resilience."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Cost overruns typical of FMIS projects may exhaust the US$50 M budget, jeopardizing component delivery.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement strict cost monitoring, use phased procurement, and reserve contingency funds within the budget envelope.",
      "evidence": "Lesson learned (Section 33‑34): FMIS projects often costly and lengthy."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Delayed adoption of IPSAS could limit improvements in financial reporting and external audit quality.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set a clear IPSAS adoption timeline, provide technical assistance, and monitor progress through quarterly reports.",
      "evidence": "Component 1.1 activity (i): adopting IPSAS to improve reporting."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Insufficient gender‑budget tagging may fail to meet gender‑responsive objectives and attract criticism.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Expand training for municipal finance officers, set incremental targets, and link funding to gender‑tagging compliance.",
      "evidence": "Section 39‑40: only 0.6 % of budget gender‑tagged; low municipal adoption."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Limited coordination with IMF and IDB on IPSAS and data integration could cause duplicated efforts or gaps.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish a joint coordination committee, share work plans, and align timelines with partner agencies.",
      "evidence": "Section 31‑32: IMF leading IPSAS roadmap; IDB improving data quality."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Inadequate monitoring and evaluation capacity may prevent timely detection of implementation problems.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Staff a dedicated M&E specialist, adopt the results framework, and conduct mid‑term independent evaluation.",
      "evidence": "Section 36‑38: PIU will establish monitoring system; interim evaluation before mid‑term review."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Fiscal constraints and reliance on volatile remittance‑driven revenues could limit ability to sustain reforms.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Phase reforms to prioritize low‑cost high‑impact actions and build fiscal buffers through efficiency savings.",
      "evidence": "Section 7‑8: remittances 19.4 % of GDP; decline would reduce VAT collections."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Procurement of ICT hardware may face delays due to compliance with World Bank procurement regulations.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Prepare detailed procurement plans early, use pre‑qualified vendors, and align with World Bank procurement guidelines.",
      "evidence": "Section 53: procurement will follow World Bank Regulations; detailed procedures required."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Low adoption of predictive analytics limits potential efficiency gains from data‑driven budgeting.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Invest in advanced analytics tools, pilot predictive models in one sector, and scale based on results.",
      "evidence": "Section 10‑11: 96 % use descriptive analytics; predictive analytics minimal."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Cyberattacks could compromise PFM information systems, causing data loss, service disruption and loss of public trust.
risks.mitigation: Implement ISO‑27000 ISMS, establish a CSIRT and SOC, conduct regular penetration testing and staff cyber‑security training.
risks.evidence: Section 10‑11: multiple cyber‑attacks on tax authority (2021), Foreign Ministry (2022), Guatecompras (2023).

risks.description: Delay in establishing the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) may postpone disbursements and stall reform activities.
risks.mitigation: Set a firm deadline, monitor PIU staffing weekly, and include PIU establishment as a withdrawal condition with Bank oversight.
risks.evidence: Condition: No withdrawal until PIU is established (Section ‘Conditions’, withdrawal condition).

risks.description: Fragmented and non‑interoperable legacy IFMIS and peripheral systems could hinder data integration and efficiency gains.
risks.mitigation: Adopt a phased integration roadmap, use open standards, and conduct interoperability testing before full rollout.
risks.evidence: Section 9‑10: fragmentation, manual processes, lack of transactional integration between SICOIN and Guatecompras.

risks.description: Insufficient data governance and analytics capacity may limit the use of data‑driven decision‑making.
risks.mitigation: Create a data governance model, establish a dedicated analytics unit, and deliver structured training for data analysts.
risks.evidence: Section 9‑10: weak data governance, limited analytical capacity, lack of structured career paths.

risks.description: High staff turnover and weak institutional stability could erode reform ownership and continuity.
risks.mitigation: Secure senior‑level commitment, institutionalize reform champions, and implement incentive mechanisms for key staff.
risks.evidence: Lesson learned (Section 32): lack of preparation and institutional stability caused past reform failures.

risks.description: Political commitment may wane, leading to reduced support for PFM reforms and possible policy reversals.
risks.mitigation: Engage high‑level officials through regular briefings, embed reforms in legal frameworks, and build a coalition of ministries.

risks.description: Extreme weather events could damage ICT infrastructure, interrupt system operations and delay implementation.

risks.evidence: Section 44‑46: climate risks identified; need for business continuity and resilience.

risks.description: Cost overruns typical of FMIS projects may exhaust the US$50 M budget, jeopardizing component delivery.

risks.description: Delayed adoption of IPSAS could limit improvements in financial reporting and external audit quality.

risks.evidence: Component 1.1 activity (i): adopting IPSAS to improve reporting.

risks.description: Insufficient gender‑budget tagging may fail to meet gender‑responsive objectives and attract criticism.

risks.description: Limited coordination with IMF and IDB on IPSAS and data integration could cause duplicated efforts or gaps.

risks.evidence: Section 31‑32: IMF leading IPSAS roadmap; IDB improving data quality.

risks.description: Inadequate monitoring and evaluation capacity may prevent timely detection of implementation problems.
risks.mitigation: Staff a dedicated M&E specialist, adopt the results framework, and conduct mid‑term independent evaluation.
risks.evidence: Section 36‑38: PIU will establish monitoring system; interim evaluation before mid‑term review.

risks.description: Fiscal constraints and reliance on volatile remittance‑driven revenues could limit ability to sustain reforms.
risks.mitigation: Phase reforms to prioritize low‑cost high‑impact actions and build fiscal buffers through efficiency savings.
risks.evidence: Section 7‑8: remittances 19.4 % of GDP; decline would reduce VAT collections.

risks.description: Procurement of ICT hardware may face delays due to compliance with World Bank procurement regulations.
risks.mitigation: Prepare detailed procurement plans early, use pre‑qualified vendors, and align with World Bank procurement guidelines.
risks.evidence: Section 53: procurement will follow World Bank Regulations; detailed procedures required.

risks.description: Low adoption of predictive analytics limits potential efficiency gains from data‑driven budgeting.
risks.mitigation: Invest in advanced analytics tools, pilot predictive models in one sector, and scale based on results.
risks.evidence: Section 10‑11: 96 % use descriptive analytics; predictive analytics minimal.
